This file documents the lei_bic resource at the shell, one section per command. Every command is a subcommand of =lei_bic=, and every section exports its own script into =projects/ores.shell/scripts/library/=. Loading a script runs that one command, so a failure names the command it came from.

* Commands

** =list=
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: 3D948633-521A-5D4A-9DE7-B659288BF9DA
:END:

Reads one page of the collection. Nothing addresses it but the caller's tenant, so it is the read that shows what exists.


The command is shaped like this:

#+begin_example
lei_bic list [--offset <n>] [--limit <n>] [--order <field>] [--desc]
#+end_example

It is addressed at =dq.v1.lei_bic.list=.

#+name: lei_bic-list
#+begin_src ores-shell :tangle lei_bic-list.ores :exports none
lei_bic list --limit 1
#+end_src

** =get=
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: 48D4E98E-BE00-55A2-9358-F65765B628AE
:END:

Reads the one row its key addresses. A key states every identifying column, so a partial key is refused rather than answered with an arbitrary row.


The command is shaped like this:

#+begin_example
lei_bic get <lei>
#+end_example

It is addressed at =dq.v1.lei_bic.get=.

#+name: lei_bic-get
#+begin_src ores-shell :tangle lei_bic-get.ores :exports none
lei_bic get __none__
#+end_src

** =get-many=
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: 3A21C7C4-A617-51E9-8511-58049B3FB7F5
:END:

Reads several rows in one request, one key group per row.


The command is shaped like this:

#+begin_example
lei_bic get-many <lei>
#+end_example

It is addressed at =dq.v1.lei_bic.get_many=.

#+name: lei_bic-get-many
#+begin_src ores-shell :tangle lei_bic-get-many.ores :exports none
